start_intro: You are the reactor operator. Keep the plant inside its envelope, follow grid demand and master the faults.
reactor_pwr_desc: Two separate loops, 158 bar, no boiling in the core. Power is set with control rods and boric acid. Every feedback is negative — forgiving, but slow to respond.
reactor_bwr_desc: A single loop, steam goes straight to the turbine. Recirculation flow moves power within seconds. At low flow and high power the density-wave instability is waiting.
reactor_rbmk_desc: Graphite moderated, pressure tubes, no full-pressure containment. At low power the void coefficient turns positive. The operating reactivity margin ORM is not a statistic, it is your life insurance.
glossary_intro: The key terms in short — not a course, just a reference.
gl_reactivity_d: How far the core sits from a self-sustaining steady chain reaction. Positive means power is rising on its own. pcm (hundred-thousandths) is the physical unit; $ (dollars) measures the same value relative to the delayed-neutron fraction — at 1 $ the chain reaction goes "prompt critical" (see there).
gl_period_d: Time for power to change by a factor of e (≈2.72). Short and positive means trouble is close. Infinite means stable.
gl_prompt_d: Reactivity reaches the delayed-neutron fraction (β, usually 1 $). From here the chain reaction sustains itself on prompt neutrons alone — power no longer rises over seconds, but over milliseconds.
gl_dnbr_d: Margin to the boiling crisis: how much power is left before the coolant film on the fuel cladding dries out completely and cooling breaks down. DNBR on the pressurized-water design, CPR on the two boiling ones — below 1 the limit is crossed.
gl_subcooling_d: Margin of coolant temperature below the saturation temperature at the current pressure. As it falls toward zero, the coolant starts boiling where the design never intended it to.
gl_xenon_d: Xe-135 builds up during operation and absorbs neutrons. After a power cut it keeps building for hours, fed by the decay of its precursor iodine-135 — reactivity keeps falling before it recovers.
gl_samarium_d: Sm-149 acts like xenon but is stable — it doesn't decay away, it has to be burned out by fissioning. After a long shutdown the poisoning just sits there instead of fading.
gl_orm_d: On the RBMK: how many control rods, in rod-equivalents, are still in the core. Not just a readout — it's the parameter that sets the void coefficient. The emptier the core, the more positive its response to boiling.
gl_void_d: How reactivity responds to steam voids in the coolant. Negative (pressurized- and boiling-water designs) is self-limiting: more steam means less reactivity. Positive (RBMK at low operating margin) is self-reinforcing.
gl_doppler_d: As fuel temperature rises, the U-238 resonances broaden and absorb more neutrons — always negative, acts instantly, and the fastest built-in brake on all three plant types.
gl_decay_d: Heat from the radioactive decay of fission products, which keeps going even after a scram — starting around 7% of rated power, then fading slowly over hours and days. The reason a shut-down core still needs cooling.
gl_scram_d: Reactor trip: every rod drives in at maximum speed. Named differently by control room — RESA in German, SCRAM in American usage, AZ-5 on the RBMK. Never fires on its own — what a given alarm means is in its own help text on the annunciator.
gl_annun_d: New (fast blink + horn): just came in, unacknowledged. Acknowledged (steady light): seen, cause still present. Cleared (slow blink): cause gone, but not yet acknowledged. Dark: everything normal.
empty_stage: This area is filled in a later version.
fault_body: The simulation reached an invalid state and was stopped. That is a bug in the game, not your mistake.
footer_note: Physically modelled, but a game — not a training simulator.
reactor_soon_hint: This type arrives in a later version. The pressurised water reactor is already playable.
ctl_boron_hint: Takes about three minutes to arrive.
trip_power_high_help: Reactor power above 112% – trip the reactor now. Usually caused by pulling rods too fast or a load step; ramp back up more slowly afterwards.
trip_period_short_help: Reactor period too short, power rising too fast – trip the reactor before the power limit is exceeded. Move the rods more slowly next time, or leave them on automatic.
trip_pzr_press_low_help: Pressurizer pressure too low – trip the reactor. Usually a leak or too much spray; afterwards check the pressurizer heaters and don't overdo boron/feedwater injection.
trip_pzr_press_high_help: Pressurizer pressure too high – trip the reactor. Usually too little spray during a power rise, or a stuck relief valve; afterwards ramp power more slowly.
trip_pzr_level_low_help: Pressurizer level falling – a warning ahead of the pressure trip. Check feedwater/boron injection and slow the power rise.
trip_dnbr_low_help: Margin to the boiling crisis (DNBR) undercut – trip the reactor. Power is too high for the available coolant flow; afterwards ramp power back up more slowly and keep all pumps running.
trip_sg_level_low_help: Steam generator level too low – trip the reactor, or risk the feedwater pumps. Check the feedwater control (automatic) or raise the feedwater valve by hand.
alarm_sg_level_high_help: Steam generator level too high – risk of water carrying over into the steam line. Throttle back feedwater.
alarm_sg_press_high_help: Steam pressure in the steam generator high – governor valve not opening enough, or power too high for the steam demand. Check the valve or lower power.
trip_rcp_lost_help: Reactor coolant pump(s) lost – trip the reactor, flow is no longer enough. Check pump status and restart the failed pump.
alarm_subcool_low_help: Subcooling margin low – approaching saturation. Raise pressure or lower power before DNBR is undercut.
alarm_porv_open_help: Pressurizer relief valve open – bleeding off pressure; sustained flow means coolant loss. Fix the cause (pressure too high); the valve should reseat on its own.
alarm_turbine_trip_help: Turbine has tripped – no more load is being taken. Check power and grid output and stabilize the plant before reconnecting.
trip_clad_temp_help: Cladding temperature too high – fuel at risk, trip the reactor now. Afterwards keep power well below the design limit and make sure coolant flow is available.
end_destroyed_body: Fuel enthalpy exceeded 963 J/g. The fuel is dispersed, the plant is lost.
trip_dome_press_high_help: Reactor vessel dome pressure too high – trip the reactor. Check the turbine valve/bypass and increase steam offtake.
trip_level_low_help: Level too low – trip the reactor, core coverage at risk. Raise feedwater and check the feedwater control (automatic).
alarm_level_high_help: Level too high – risk of water carrying over into the steam system/turbine. Throttle back feedwater.
trip_oprm_help: Power oscillation detected (OPRM) – trip the reactor. Usually caused by low recirculation flow at high power; next time raise recirc flow in time or lower power.
alarm_instability_help: Signs of a power oscillation – raise recirculation flow or lower power before the OPRM trip fires.
alarm_recirc_low_help: Recirculation flow low – instability risk at high power. Speed up the recirculation pumps or pull power back.
alarm_msiv_closed_help: Main steam isolation valves closed – no steam to the turbine, reactor pressure rising. Clear the cause; only reopen once cleared.
alarm_srv_open_help: Safety/relief valve has lifted – bleeding off pressure. Fix the cause (pressure too high); the valve should reseat on its own.
alarm_orm_low_help: Operating reactivity margin (ORM) low – too few rods in the core for a safe shutdown. Insert rods, don't withdraw further, and hold power.
alarm_orm_critical_help: Operating reactivity margin critically low – high risk of a positive reactivity insertion on shutdown. Insert rods and lower power immediately.
alarm_void_positive_help: Void coefficient strongly positive – falling coolant flow or boiling will drive reactivity up on its own. Secure recirculation flow and avoid running at low power.
alarm_mcp_cavitation_help: Main circulation pumps cavitating – flow and cooling at risk. Lower recirculation flow or check drum pressure/level.
alarm_graphite_hot_help: Graphite temperature high – lower power so the moderator doesn't overheat.
alarm_axial_tilt_help: Axial power tilt – uneven rod positions. Even out the rods / re-align them symmetrically.
az5_hint: AZ-5 drives every rod in over 18 seconds — graphite tips first.
scn_free_desc: No orders, no score. The plant is yours.
scn_pwr_load_follow_brief: The grid ramps down over midday and back up in the afternoon. Keep generator output inside the demand curve. Somewhere in this shift a rod bank jams — then only boron is left, and boron takes three minutes.
scn_pwr_turbine_trip_brief: Ten minutes in, the turbine trips. The reactor still has to shed its heat: steam dumps, pressuriser, steam generator level. Shortly after, feedwater control fails too.
scn_bwr_flow_brief: Three hours of load following, done with recirculation flow instead of rods. Watch the decay ratio: high power at low flow is the excluded corner of the map.
scn_bwr_msiv_brief: Seven minutes in, the isolation valves shut. Pressure rises, the voids collapse, reactivity goes positive. You have seconds.
scn_rbmk_night_brief: Power is to come down to 200 MW and back up later. Xenon builds, the reactivity margin melts away. Below 30 rods operation is forbidden — and below 15, AZ-5 is no longer a scram but an ignition.
scn_pwr_porv_brief: A quiet shift at full power — until the pressurizer relief valve sticks open. Pressure and level fall, coolant slowly bleeds away. The annunciator warns early; ignore it and you lose subcooling first, then DNBR. The same failure that started Three Mile Island, 1979.
scn_bwr_instab_brief: Main recirculation flow drops back to low throughput while grid demand stays high. Chase power with the rods instead of restoring flow first, and the core drifts into the forbidden corner of the power/flow map — where the oscillation grows on its own until OPRM sounds. The trip won't fire itself.
